In the 14th century AD, during the Latin Empire of Constantinople, the city of Nea Patras was founded. It was named after the ancient Greek city of Patras, which was a significant religious center for Christianity. The new city was built to serve as a refuge for the Christian population after the fall of the Byzantine Empire.
